expected.charges: Washington sedition prosecution: conspiracy under former 18 U.S.C. § 11 to violate the Smith Act’s military-insubordination provision, former 18 U.S.C. § 9.
expected.indicted: January 3, 1944 superseding indictment naming thirty defendants.
expected.convicted: No conviction; mistrial December 7, 1944; indictment dismissed December 2, 1946.
expected.judge: Edward C. Eicher; Bolitha J. Laws (dismissal proceedings)
expected.sentence: No sentence imposed in the Washington Smith Act prosecution. Individual custody duration is not established; separate criminal convictions are not counted as Smith Act imprisonment.

updates.sentence: No sentence imposed in the Washington Smith Act prosecution. Individual custody duration is not established; separate criminal convictions are not counted as Smith Act imprisonment. The February28,1944 opinion, United States v.McWilliams,54F.Supp.791, individually lists Alderman through counsel Harry A.Grant and identifies O’John Rogge and Joseph W.Burns as the government attorneys. This pretrial ruling does not establish his custody admission or release. Source: https://case-law.vlex.com/vid/united-states-v-mcwilliams-886698831
